- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply a 1–3 day lag correction, dampening forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is falling, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 3–7% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 50-day moving average, model tends to overreact; apply a 1–2 day smoothing filter.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true price volatility; increase forecast by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model fails to adjust quickly; apply a 2–3 day “sentiment catch-up” correction to align with sentiment momentum.
